transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-24 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM); Liam O'Keefe (CTO), Maya Lopez (Head of ML), Ravi Patel (DevOps), Zoë Chen (Product)

Auto-summary (auto): Pendragon is approaching renewal; wants committed uplift + EU on-prem pilot to meet data residency. Need bench run and SOW amendment.

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — can you see my screen?
[00:06] Liam O'Keefe: yep yep seeing it, thanks sofia.
[00:10] Sofia: cool. quick agenda: renewal numbers, eu private pilot, benchmarks, security checklist. if anything to add say now.
[00:20] Maya Lopez: maybe one ask — we want to confirm p95 latency under load for our 1.2K rps mix.
[00:28] Daniel Cho: ok that’s good, we'll run a throughput bench with your prompt set. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and kv cache hit rates.
[00:38] Ravi Patel: quick infra note, our infra team wants to see VPC peering, egress and KMS design before green light.
[00:45] Priya Nair: we'll include the KMS/HSM integration doc, and SOC2 attestation pointers.

[02:05] Sofia: on renewal - you mentioned a 30% uplift committed for next period, is that still the ask?
[02:12] Liam: yes, and we want the ability to burst beyond that. can you reiterate burst policies on Dedicated vs Private?
[02:20] Daniel: sure, so dedicated reserved pools give you predictable throughput — bursts can be configured as a short-term capacity pool. private (EU on‑prem) pilot is more of a managed private control plane; burst is limited by on‑prem hardware unless we provision additional nodes. so tradeoff: cost predictability vs flexibility.
[02:45] Maya: sounds like latencies for Private are similar but depends on local hardware, quantization profile etc. we might accept slightly higher cost for local residency.

[04:10] Sofia: pricing — we'll put together three scenarios: a conservative commit, a mid-tier with burst credits, and an enterprise reserved with longer term discount.
[04:18] Liam: ok want to see those. also please show unit costs token-level; our CFO wants clear delta vs openai.
[04:27] Sofia: will do, we'll break down per-token generation and embeddings, and show caching savings.

[06:00] Daniel: on the technical side — our plan for the on‑prem pilot is a lightweight package: customer-managed nodes, Redwood private control plane, KMS integration. we need to validate model kernel selection and quantization to match your sequence lengths.
[06:18] Maya: our typical sequences are 512 tokens, many short queries but some 2k chats. how will that affect kv cache footprint?
[06:25] Daniel: larger sequences increase KV cache pressure; we recommend a two-tier cache policy — prefix caching for common prompts + session-wide KV reuse. that reduces per-token compute.
[06:40] Ravi: can you ex- — ex- explain how autoscaling would work on‑prem? is it even supported?
[06:48] Daniel: autoscale on‑prem is limited; we can orchestrate node reboots and scheduled capacity but true elastic autoscale is tied to cloud Dedicated. for on‑prem we do horizontal scaling with manual or semi-automated triggers.

[08:30] Zoë Chen: question — do you support SAML SSO + SCIM for RBAC in Private?
[08:36] Priya: yes, SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning; RBAC roles mirror hosted product; audit logs are shipped to your SIEM or stored on-prem per the pilot config.
[09:00] Liam: and encryption at rest with our KMS? can we bring our own key, HSM?
[09:05] Daniel: BYOK supported, and HSM integrations are in the pipeline — we can document current KMS flow.

[10:35] Maya: one risk — we do A/B tests and model rollouts. how do you handle rollbacks if a model regression impacts prod?
[10:42] Daniel: we have canary rollouts, A/B and automatic fallback policies to a compatible variant; Redwood Optimize can flag quality regressions against your eval set.
[11:00] Sofia: we'll include the evals and regression alert examples in the packet.

[12:15] Liam: what about compliance docs? SOC2, ISO? need a pack for procurement.
[12:22] Priya: we'll send SOC2 Type II report, encryption attestations, pen test summary and our standard data handling addendum.

[14:00] Ravi: networking again — our security team wants to know about egress IPs, private link, and whether traffic ever leaves EU during pilot.
[14:08] Daniel: with Private on‑prem, traffic stays in your cluster; control plane can be in EU region as well. we will provide egress blocklists and an architecture diagram. if you use hybrid (dedicated + private) we can route failover to EU hosted region to avoid crossing boundaries.

[16:40] Maya: about the bench: can you emulate our mix? we have 70% short prompts, 25% embeddings, 5% long chat.
[16:48] Daniel: yes, send us the prompt samples and we'll run a 24h test to capture diurnal patterns. we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token-cost.

[19:20] Liam: timeline — we want pilot in EU by end of Q3. feasible?
[19:28] Sofia: tight but doable; we need signed amendment and approval for pilot L1 infra. plan: SOW + pricing this week, bench next week, infra diagram + KMS integration concurrently, kickoff first week Sept.
[19:44] Ravi: is there a quick checklist for prerequisites so we can prep infra?
[19:49] Priya: yes I'll share a pilot readiness checklist — network rules, nodes spec, certs, KMS endpoint.

[22:10] Zoë: procurement question — if we extend earlier, are penalties/credits pro-rated?
[22:16] Sofia: we'll provide options; one scenario keeps current billing cadence and adds uplift prorated to effective date; the enterprise scenario has a credit clause for availability under SLA. we'll put options in the amendment.

[24:00] Maya: any known issues with model compatibility for quantized variants? we run some custom tokenizers.
[24:08] Daniel: custom tokenizers can be onboarded but we need to validate tokenization parity. quantization may change output distribution slightly; we recommend running your eval prompts against both FP16 and quant variants.

[27:05] Liam: competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and OpenAI pricing, also an internal POC on SageMaker. main tie-breaker is latency and predictability.
[27:16] Sofia: understood; we'll show head-to-head up front with token-level compute and caching impact, and a failover plan.

[30:00] Daniel: one technical caveat — on‑prem debugging traces are more limited than hosted; we provide a tracing agent and token-level logs but we can't ingest into Redwood hosted analytics unless you allow.
[30:12] Ravi: fine, we'll keep logs local. how about retention?
[30:16] Priya: retention configurable; for pilot we recommend 30 days by default, can extend.

[34:00] Sofia: recap — deliverables: SOW + three pricing scenarios, bench run with your prompts, pilot readiness checklist, security pack. next call we'll review bench and pick a pricing path.
[34:15] Liam: good. can we get the SOW by Friday?
[34:20] Sofia: yes, by Friday EOD.

[36:45] Maya: quick note — we'd like a short runbook for rollout, i.e., how will rollback happen under traffic?
[36:52] Daniel: we'll deliver a rollback playbook with step-by-step commands, and a canary strategy tuned to your traffic.

[39:30] Sofia: ok thanks everyone. last check: any blockers we didn't cover?
[39:36] Ravi: none from infra side after we get the VPC diagram.
[39:40] Zoë: procurement waits on SOC2 pack.
[39:43] Liam: sounds good. thanks all.

Meeting close: 15:42 UTC.

Recap (auto): Redwood to provide SOW + pricing, run benchmark with prompt set, share security materials and pilot checklist. Follow up deep-dive for VPC on 2026-09-02.
